title: Pull or push?

controls.label: AD shift (billions at every price level)
SRAS shift (billions at every price level)

predict.q: The economy starts in long-run equilibrium: price level **110**, real output **2,000** (potential). One change pushes the price level up to **115**. Another change does the same. What tells you which one happened?

options.s: Nothing: both shifts give exactly the same new equilibrium
options.fb: The price level is the same, but look at real output: 2,075 after the AD shift, 1,950 after the SRAS shift. Output is the clue.

options.s: Real output: it rises after a rise in AD and falls after a fall in SRAS
options.fb: AD +125: price level 115, output 2,075. SRAS −125: price level 115, output 1,950.

options.s: Real output: it falls after a rise in AD and rises after a fall in SRAS
options.fb: A rise in AD moves the economy up along SRAS, so output rises. Higher costs move it up along AD, so output falls.

task: Move AD right by **125**, reset, then move SRAS left by **125**. Watch real output and unemployment.

target.do: Move AD to +125 (or SRAS to −125), then press Check. Use Reset to try the other.

takeaway: Both raise the price level by about **4.5%**. Demand-pull comes with **more** output; cost-push with **less**.
